raw_response:
Aiya, let me think about this year. I'm 73 now, been doing wheat-maize on this little patch for 40 years. Only 3.1 mu — half a mu here, a strip there. My son and daughter-in-law work in town most of the year, so mostly it's me and the old lady in the field. The grandkids help on weekends sometimes.

**For the wheat** (already in the ground since October) —
I planted the usual local variety, the one our village agent brings around, maybe 15 yuan worth of seed per mu. Before planting I spread about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (that diammonium stuff, 复合肥) across the wheat ground, that's roughly 40 kg per mu of the compound. Comes out to maybe 12-13 kg of nitrogen per mu from the base. 

Come spring now — the wheat is greening up — I'll topdress with urea when I irrigate. Usually I do about half a bag of urea per mu, so maybe another 10 kg of N. My neighbor old Wang says this year looks a bit dry so we'll probably need to water 3 times: now at greening, then at jointing, and once more at grain filling if the rain doesn't come. The well is metered, costs me maybe 30 yuan a mu each time. I can't afford 5 waterings like the big farms do.

Pesticides — I'll spray once for aphids when I see them, and a weed spray early. My son buys the bottles from the shop in town, not expensive.

Harvest around early June. I pay the combine man — he comes through the village, charges about 50 yuan per mu now. Can't cut 3 mu by hand anymore, not at my age.

**For the maize** after wheat —
Very tight turnaround, maybe 3-4 days between combine and planting. I hire the planter-guy, he does no-till direct seeding right into the wheat stubble, 30 yuan per mu. Seed is hybrid, whatever the agricultural store pushes — costs about 40-50 yuan per mu for the seed.

At planting the planter drops about 1.5 bags of compound fertilizer per mu with the seed. Then at big-bellmouth stage (大喇叭口) I topdress urea, about half a bag per mu. That's how I've always done it. Total maybe 15 kg N per mu for the maize.

Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat here — if it rains in July-August like usual I might not water at all. If dry, one watering at tasseling. 

One herbicide spray after planting for the weeds. Sometimes borer, sometimes not — I'll look.

Harvest late September, early October. Combine again, then the planter-guy comes back to put the wheat in. Round and round it goes, 40 years the same.

**Why I don't do more** — money is tight. My old-age allowance isn't much. The kids send some but they have their own lives. I stick with what works. Old Li down the road tried that new variety two years back and lost half his crop. No thanks. I'll do what I did last year.
